newsitem.title: UK: London gold buoyant with sharply higher silver.
newsitem.headline: London gold buoyant with sharply higher silver.

text.p: Gold prices were sharply higher on Tuesday morning, boosted by strength in silver and fresh European buying.
Silver, which broke above $5.00 an ounce late on Monday for the first time since last October, was quieter than gold but holding comfortably above that key level, dealers said.
Gold fixed at $357.25 an ounce, compared to $353.60 on Monday afternoon and a London close of $354.45/$354.95.
The fixing was the highest since January 14 and up nearly $10 from a last week's low fixing of $348.
Silver's dramatic 30-cent rally over the past few days, attributed to fund buying and a play on the gold-silver ratio, had lent strength to the gold market in New York and Asian markets.
One dealer also suggested producer buy-backs had helped boost the gold price.
"There's been more buying in gold this morning, a lot of which is options related," a dealer said, referring to the expiry of over-the-counter options on Wednesday.
Prices are likely going to be capped in the near term at $358, where stiff technical resistance was seen, analysts said.
Beyond there, the $360 area was a key retracement level from gold's recent 3-1/4 year lows.
But by Wednesday's expiry, several dealers said, prices were likely to ease back to $355, an area of significant interest for options holders.
Longer term, gold's fundamentals still looked soggy and prices may yet revisit recent lows, dealers and analysts said.
Silver, indicated at $5.03/$5.05, was up just one cent from Monday's firm London close and showing less spark than in recent days.
"Silver's a bit sluggish this morning. It's still bullish and leading the trend, but gold is holding its own right now," a dealer said.
The $5.00 level was psychological but the break above it was also a breach of a one-year downtrend, boding well for more upside moves, technical analysts said.
On the upside $5.10 was expected to provide resistance, but $5.25 was also mentioned as a potential near term target.
Platinum was moderately firmer with gold and silver at $360.50/$361.50.
But palladium was barely changed at $122.75/$123.75.
